title: Payment methods in Singapore: what to accept and what they cost
summary: PayNow, cards, GrabPay, ShopeePay and BNPL in Singapore compared by fee, online and in store. Rates checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** The most-used payment methods in Singapore are PayNow, credit and debit cards, and e-wallets such as GrabPay, plus BNPL. With HitPay you can accept them online and in store on one account. PayNow is 0.65% + S$0.30 from S$100, or 0.9% (min S$0.20) below S$100, and domestic cards are 2.8% + S$0.50, with no setup or monthly fees.


Most Singapore customers pay with PayNow, cards (including Apple Pay and Google Pay) or GrabPay, so those are the methods to accept first. Here is what each one is for and what it costs on HitPay's published rates, so you can decide what to switch on.

## PayNow and SGQR


PayNow is Singapore's real-time bank transfer. Customers scan a QR in their banking app, and the money arrives in real time.


### What is SGQR?


SGQR is Singapore's unified QR label. One code works across many payment apps, including PayNow.[The Singapore Quick Response code (SGQR)](https://www.imda.gov.sg/resources/press-releases-factsheets-and-speeches/archived/imda/press-releases/2018/singapore-introduces-world-first-unified-payment-qr-code-sgqr) was launched in 2018 to make accepting in-person QR code payments easier. Display one code at your counter, and customers scan it with the payment app they already use.


### PayNow fees on HitPay


Online 0.65% + S$0.30 (S$100 and above); 0.9%, min S$0.20 (below S$100); in person 0.4%, min S$0.10.


[Accept PayNow →](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/paynow) ·[Static QR for your counter →](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/static-qr)


## Cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay


Cards are still expected at checkout, especially for higher-value orders and overseas buyers. Domestic cards online cost 2.8% + S$0.50. International cards cost 3.65% + S$0.50, plus 2% on foreign-currency transactions.


American Express is accepted by HitPay at the same card rates, and is relevant for premium retail, corporate accounts, and travel businesses.


Cards also underpin Apple Pay and Google Pay: when a customer taps their phone at a terminal, the payment runs on the underlying card credential — so your card acceptance automatically covers these wallet methods.


Apple Pay and Google Pay are contactless wallet methods that use device-stored card credentials. They are accepted wherever your card terminals support NFC contactless payment — no separate integration required. For online checkout, both are supported via HitPay's hosted payment page. These methods are particularly valued for their speed at the point of sale: no PIN entry required for many transactions.


3D Secure (3DS) authentication is built into HitPay's card processing. This adds a layer of fraud protection and shifts liability for fraudulent transactions to the card issuer, protecting merchants from a significant category of chargeback.[Accept cards with 3D Secure on the HitPay payment gateway →](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/payment-gateway)


## Digital wallets: GrabPay, ShopeePay, WeChat Pay


Digital wallets are a distinct payment category in Singapore, sitting between bank transfers and traditional cards. They are app-based, quick to use, and often tied to loyalty rewards — which drives strong repeat usage.


GrabPay is Singapore's dominant super-app wallet, used by Grab's large regional user base. Customers load funds or link a card to their GrabPay account. For merchants, GrabPay acceptance opens the door to Grab's rewards-driven ecosystem, where users are often motivated to pay via Grab to earn GrabRewards points. HitPay charges 3% for GrabPay.


ShopeePay is Shopee's integrated payment wallet, heavily used by the Shopee shopping platform's user base. As with GrabPay, customers earn loyalty points for paying via ShopeePay. For HitPay's ShopeePay rate,[see /sg/pricing](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/pricing) .


WeChat Pay is the cross-border wallet most Chinese visitors use. HitPay charges 1.5% for WeChat Pay.


Accept GrabPay, ShopeePay, Apple Pay and Google Pay at checkout:[see the HitPay payment gateway →](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/payment-gateway)

Atome, Paylater by Grab and ShopeePay Later let customers split payments, and you're paid upfront. Paylater by Grab is 5.5% on HitPay. Atome and ShopeePay Later:[see /sg/pricing](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/pricing) .

## How to start accepting them


### E-commerce plugins


Merchants on[Shopify](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/shopify) , WooCommerce or Wix can install a HitPay plugin and switch on payment methods. No custom code is required.


### Payment links


For businesses without a dedicated website,[payment links](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/payment-links) are the most practical entry point. Send one by WhatsApp, email or SMS, and the customer clicks and pays.


### QR codes


A[static QR code](https://hitpayapp.com/sg/static-qr) at the counter lets customers pay with PayNow without cash or a card machine.


### API


Businesses building a custom storefront or marketplace can integrate through the[HitPay payment API](https://hitpayapp.com/paymentapis) . It gives the most control over checkout but needs development resource.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the most popular payment methods in Singapore?


For most Singapore businesses the core set is PayNow, Visa and Mastercard cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay, and GrabPay. Many also add buy now, pay later options such as Atome or Paylater by Grab, and WeChat Pay or UPI for visitors.


### What is the cheapest payment method for Singapore merchants?


On HitPay's published rates, PayNow is usually the cheapest online method: 0.65% + S$0.30 for orders of S$100 and above, and 0.9% (minimum S$0.20) below S$100. In person, PayNow is 0.4% (minimum S$0.10). Domestic cards online are 2.8% + S$0.50.


### Is PayNow or credit card cheaper for merchants?


PayNow is cheaper on HitPay's published rates. On a S$200 order, PayNow costs S$1.60 (0.65% + S$0.30) and a domestic card costs S$6.10 (2.8% + S$0.50).


### What is SGQR?


SGQR is Singapore's unified QR code standard. One SGQR label lets customers scan with many payment apps, including PayNow. HitPay's static QR lets you display one code at the counter and receive payments into your HitPay account.


### Do I need separate accounts for each payment method?


No. With HitPay you can accept PayNow, cards, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, WeChat Pay and UPI from one account, with no setup fee and no monthly fee.


### What payment methods should a new Singapore online store start with?


Start with PayNow and cards (including Apple Pay and Google Pay), since most customers use these. Add GrabPay and a buy now, pay later option if your average order is higher or your customers are younger shoppers.


### Can I accept payments from tourists in Singapore?


Yes. Online, international cards work at 3.65% + S$0.50, plus 2% on foreign-currency transactions. In store, HitPay's Borderless QR lets visitors pay with wallets from home, such as WeChat Pay, UPI, DuitNow, PromptPay, QR Ph and GCash.


### Does HitPay charge monthly fees for accepting multiple payment methods?


No. HitPay has no setup fee and no monthly fee. You pay a published fee per transaction for each method.


### What is the cheapest payment method for businesses in Singapore?


PayNow is usually cheapest. On HitPay, a S$20 online PayNow sale costs S$0.20 versus S$1.06 by domestic card (2.8% + S$0.50).


### Should I accept BNPL in Singapore?


BNPL such as Atome (5.5%) and PayLater by Grab (5.5% online) costs more, so it suits higher-ticket items where it lifts basket size.
